subtitle: How a Ganga general carved humility into a hill of stone

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide from the hilltop, framing the colossal stone Bahubali behind a small, determined Chavundaraya
panels.action: Chavundaraya stands on the bare granite of Vindhyagiri, hands folded, as the colossal, serene stone form of Bahubali looms unfinished behind him, the plains of Shravanabelagola fading into mist below.

dialogue.text: In the late 10th century, a Ganga general named Chavundaraya turned a rocky hill into Bahubali himself—why did a man of war choose to carve the very image of renunciation?

i18n.hi: दसवीं सदी के अंत में गंगा सेनापति चामुंडराय ने एक नंगी चट्टान को खुद बाहुबली बना दिया—युद्धवीर ने विराग की मूर्ति क्यों تراशी?

panels.shot: broad aerial establishing shot of Karnataka’s rolling hills and tanks, early morning haze
panels.action: The twin hills of Shravanabelagola rise from the Deccan plain, one crowned with a tiny shrine, the other still raw and bare, a shimmering lake nestled between them.

dialogue.text: On the Deccan plateau, between the twin hills of Chandragiri and Vindhyagiri, a Jain centre quietly grew under the Western Gangas as kings rose and fell around it.

i18n.hi: दक्खिन के पठार पर, चंद्रगिरि और विंध्यगिरि के बीच, पश्चिमी गंगाओं के समय जैन केन्द्र चुपचाप बढ़ा, जबकि चारों ओर राजाएं उठे और ढहे.

panels.shot: medium interior shot in a royal court, slightly low angle on Chavundaraya
panels.action: In a candlelit Ganga court, Chavundaraya stands in armour beside the throne, one hand on his sword hilt, the other holding a palm-leaf manuscript, counsellors and monks in the background.

dialogue.text: Chavundaraya served the late Ganga rulers as general and minister—his hand knew the weight of steel, his mind the weight of scripture and numbers.

i18n.hi: चामुंडराय गंगा राजाओं के लिए सेनापति और मंत्री रहा—उसके हाथ ने लोहा उठाया, दिमाग ने धर्म और गणना दोनों संभाली.

panels.shot: close-up on Chavundaraya’s face, half in shadow between battlefield and shrine reflections
panels.action: Chavundaraya’s weathered face is split by shadow; behind one shoulder, a faint ghost-image of marching soldiers; behind the other, a quiet Jain monk seated in meditation.

dialogue.speaker: chavundaraya
dialogue.text: Victory over others is easy. How does one carve victory over the self?

i18n.hi: दूसरों पर जीत आसान है। अपने आप पर जीत कैसे تراशें?

panels.shot: wide shot atop Chandragiri, camera behind Chavundaraya looking toward Vindhyagiri
panels.action: From a small shrine on Chandragiri, Chavundaraya stands looking across the lake toward the bare mass of Vindhyagiri, monks and lay followers around him, flags fluttering in the wind.

dialogue.text: Shravanabelagola’s inscriptions remember him here, moving between Chandragiri’s shrines and Vindhyagiri’s bare stone, his devotion turning into a plan.

i18n.hi: श्रवणबेलगोला के शिलालेख उसे यहीं याद करते हैं—चंद्रगिरि के मंदिरों से विंध्यगिरि की नंगी चट्टान तक, उसकी भक्ति धीरे‑धीरे योजना बन गई.

panels.shot: medium shot in a simple hall, Chavundaraya seated before Jain teachers, overhead perspective
panels.action: In a pillared hall, Chavundaraya sits respectfully before Jain ācāryas, a palm-leaf of the story of Bahubali spread open on the floor between them.

dialogue.text: The Jain teachers told him of Bahubali, who dropped his kingdom and stood motionless in meditation until vines climbed his legs and pride fell away.

i18n.hi: जैन आचार्यों ने उसे बाहुबली की कथा सुनाई—जिसने राज्य छोड़ दिया, ध्यान में अचल खड़ा रहा, जब तक लताएं पैरों पर चढ़ीं और अहं मिट गया.

panels.shot: steady medium close-up of Chavundaraya listening intently, candlelight flickering
panels.action: Candlelight catches Chavundaraya’s eyes as he leans forward, gripped by the tale, a faint imagined vision of Bahubali standing in meditation forming behind him.

dialogue.speaker: chavundaraya
dialogue.text: If kings forget this story, let a hill remind them.

i18n.hi: यदि राजा यह कथा भूल जाएं, तो पहाड़ उन्हें याद दिलाए.

panels.shot: high-angle wide of Vindhyagiri with scaffolding layouts being planned on the ground
panels.action: At the foot of Vindhyagiri, Chavundaraya kneels over a rough ground-plan scratched into the dust, pointing as artisans and stone-workers stand around, the towering rock behind them.

dialogue.text: He chose Vindhyagiri’s granite spine as his canvas—a monolith in situ, not carved and hauled, but brought out of the hill itself.

i18n.hi: उसने विंध्यगिरि की ग्रेनाइट रीढ़ को अपना कैनवास चुना—यहीं खड़ा एकाश्म, न काटकर ढोया गया, बल्कि पहाड़ से ही निकाला गया देव.

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of early quarrying, slight low angle to emphasize scale
panels.action: Workers chip and wedge at the granite surface, rough steps and platforms appearing along the slope, while Chavundaraya, in simple robes, oversees with a measuring rope in hand.

dialogue.text: Archaeology still reads the labour: rock cut away, platforms raised, measurements checked and rechecked, so that a 57-foot Bahubali could stand free yet rooted in the hill.

i18n.hi: पुरातत्व आज भी श्रम पढ़ लेता है—चट्टान काटी गई, मंच उठाए गए, नाप पर नाप मिलाई गई, ताकि 57 फुट का बाहुबली मुक्त खड़ा रहे, फिर भी पहाड़ में धंसा.

panels.shot: medium shot at the statue’s feet level, scaffolding rising around the rough form
panels.action: The rough, giant feet of the emerging statue jut from the stone; bamboo scaffolding clings to the figure, artisans perched with hammers, while Chavundaraya gestures upward, calculating proportions.

dialogue.text: From the feet up, they opened the stone, keeping Jain restraint: no weapons, no ornaments, just the calm of a body that has given up all claims.

i18n.hi: पैरों से ऊपर तक पत्थर खोला गया, जैन सादगी बनाई रखी—न हथियार, न आभूषण, बस उस देह की शांति जिसने हर दावा छोड़ दिया है.

panels.shot: tight close-up of a sculptor’s hand smoothing stone, Chavundaraya blurred in background
panels.action: A sculptor’s hand runs a polishing stone along the smooth thigh of the colossus, the surface catching light, while a blurred Chavundaraya in the background checks a palm-leaf sketch.

dialogue.text: Settar’s study notes the careful finishing—the skin of the stone made almost soft to the eye, the face carved with a restraint that lets silence speak.

i18n.hi: सेत्तर के अध्ययन में उस महीन घिसावट का जिक्र है—पत्थर की त्वचा आँखों को कोमल लगे, चेहरा ऐसा सधा हो कि खुद सन्नाटा बोल उठे.

panels.shot: high wide shot of a near-complete monolith towering over tiny workers
panels.action: The nearly complete Bahubali stands immense, hair in shoulder-length locks, creepers carved along his legs; tiny workers tidy scaffolds around his feet as Chavundaraya stands dwarfed at the base.

dialogue.text: Hegewald and others read the iconography: the loosened hair, the vines on the legs, the unclothed, unarmed body—signs of a king who walked away from conquest.

i18n.hi: हेगेवाल्ड व अन्य विद्वान मूर्ति के संकेत पढ़ते हैं—ढीले बाल, पैरों पर लताएं, निर्वस्त्र, निरस्त्र देह—एक ऐसे राजा की निशानियाँ जो विजय छोड़ कर चल पड़ा.

panels.shot: medium shot of Chavundaraya consulting an inscription being incised
panels.action: At a stone slab near the hill, an engraver bends to chisel a Kannada inscription as Chavundaraya dictates, another assistant holding a palm-leaf with the drafted text.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions on Vindhyagiri and Chandragiri fix his name beside the image, tying Chavundaraya’s worldly rank to this other kind of monument.

i18n.hi: विंध्यगिरि और चंद्रगिरि के शिलालेख उसकी नामपट्टी मूर्ति के पास जड़ते हैं—चामुंडराय की सांसारिक पदवी को इस दूसरी तरह की स्मारक से बाँधते हुए.

panels.shot: sunrise wide shot of the completed statue with crowds gathering for consecration
panels.action: At dawn, the finished Bahubali gleams in the soft light, platforms built around his shoulders, a gathering of monks, rulers and villagers climbing the hill in long processions.

dialogue.text: Around 981 or 983 CE, the colossus was consecrated, the hill turned into a tirtha where power and renunciation were made to meet in stone.

i18n.hi: लगभग 981 या 983 ई. में इस विराट प्रतिमा का अभिषेक हुआ—पहाड़ी तीर्थ बन गई, जहाँ शक्ति और विराग को पत्थर में मिलाया गया.

panels.shot: medium close-up of Chavundaraya at the base of the statue, hands raised in devotion
panels.action: Below the towering feet, Chavundaraya stands with joined palms, face uplifted, garlands and vessels piled around him, courtiers watching their general bow before a naked ascetic form.

dialogue.speaker: chavundaraya
dialogue.text: May this stone remind even generals that pride is heavier than granite.

i18n.hi: यह पत्थर सेनापतियों को भी याद दिलाए कि अहं ग्रेनाइट से ज्यादा भारी है.

panels.shot: dramatic medium shot of the Mahamastakabhisheka in progress on scaffolds, viewed slightly from below
panels.action: From below, we see priests on scaffolds pouring streams of liquid over Bahubali’s head, the stone darkening and shining, while crowds press at the hill’s edge and Chavundaraya watches solemnly.

dialogue.text: The first anointings began then; later centuries would call it Mahamastakabhisheka, the great head-anointing, repeated roughly every twelve years as memory itself made ritual.

i18n.hi: पहले अभिषेक तब शुरू हुए; बाद की सदियों ने इसे महामस्तकाभिषेक कहा—महान शिरो‑अभिषेक, जो हर बारह साल पर, स्मृति को ही रीति बनाकर दोहराया गया.

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of Chavundaraya slightly apart from the crowd, eyes moist, hands still folded
panels.action: Amid the festival throng, Chavundaraya stands a little apart, emotion in his eyes as he looks up at the drenched stone face of Bahubali, milk and water cascading behind him.

dialogue.text: Tradition later told the story of Gullakayajji, whose small pot of milk humbled Chavundaraya—her legend survives as a lesson that even pious patrons must kneel before simplicity.

i18n.hi: परंपरा ने बाद में गुल्लकायज्जी की कथा सुनाई—जिसके छोटे दूध के घड़े ने चामुंडराय का घमंड तोड़ा; उसकी леген्ड बताती है कि भक्त दानदाता को भी सरलता के आगे झुकना पड़ता है.

panels.shot: low-angle long shot of the statue alone as time passes, sky cycling from day to night
panels.action: The giant Bahubali stands unchanged against a sky that shifts from bright blue to starry night, faint ghost-images of later pilgrims and dynasties flickering around the hill.

dialogue.text: Empires moved on. The Gangas yielded to the Cholas and Hoysalas, but the monolith remained, its surface weathered, its quiet teaching unchanged.

i18n.hi: साम्राज्य बदलते गए। गंगे गए, चोल और होयसला आए, पर यह एकाश्म वहीं रहा—ऊपर सतह घिसी, पर उसकी शांत सीख जस की तस रही.

panels.shot: modern aerial shot of the present-day statue and crowds, echoing the opening vista
panels.action: In a contemporary view, the same Bahubali rises above a throng of present-day devotees and visitors, cameras and umbrellas dotted among saffron and white robes on the granite steps.

dialogue.text: Today, as thousands still climb Vindhyagiri and pour offerings over Bahubali’s head, they also walk in Chavundaraya’s footprint—the trace of a man who asked stone to show what humility looks like.

i18n.hi: आज भी हजारों लोग विंध्यगिरि चढ़कर बाहुबली के सिर पर अर्पण चढ़ाते हैं, तो वे चामुंडराय के पदचिह्नों पर भी चलते हैं—उस मनुष्य के, जिसने पत्थर से दिखवाया कि नम्रता कैसी दिखती है.

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Ganga general carved humility into a hill of stone
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे गंगा सेनापति ने पत्थर के पहाड़ में नम्रता गढ़ दी
